## 1. Points not under charge

No substantive point in the declared chains is listed here: the two charge lists contest their inferential links. The parties frequently quoted the same passages, but agreement on the wording did not settle the meaning assigned to it.

## 2. Link rounds and close rounds

**Status key:** *CITED-WITH-FOOTING* records that the side exhibited a chain with cited material. It is a procedural description, not a finding that the inference is established.

### Defender’s declared chain

| Link | Status | Contest and close-round result |
|---|---|---|
| **D1 — Matthew 1:18, 25** | CITED-WITH-FOOTING | The defender read “before they came together” and “knew her not till” as excluding Joseph’s participation. The challenger read the first as preceding the taking and the second as bounding abstinence from the taking to the birth. The defender repeated its reading in close. |

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures affirms that Christ was conceived in the womb of the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost without the agency of a human father, and therefore did not have a biological father.

### I. The Conception Occurred Before Joseph and Mary Came Together

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek temporal prepositional phrase translated "before they came together" contains πρίν (*prin*, G4250, "before, formerly") and συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, aorist active infinitive of συνέρχομαι, *synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together, to come together in cohabitation or conjugal union").
[L3] Matthew 1:25 confirms the absence of sexual intercourse until after the delivery: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Here "knew" renders ἔγινωσκεν (*eginōsken*, imperfect active of γινώσκω, *ginōskō*, G1097, used of carnal knowledge, as in Genesis 4:1).
[L4] Because Mary was already found with child prior to any conjugal union (*synelthein*) with Joseph, and Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth, Joseph was not the physical or biological generator of the child.

---

### II. Mary's Explicit Testimony of Carnal Inexperience

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] The Greek present active indicative verb γινώσκω (*ginōskō*, G1097, "to know, understand, perceive, have carnal relations with") is paired with the negative particle οὐ (*ou*, G3756, absolute negation) and ἄνδρα (*andra*, accusative singular of ἀνήρ, *anēr*, G435, "a male person, a husband, a man").
[L3] Genesis 19:8 exhibits the exact semantic force of knowing a man as sexual relations: "Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man."
[L4] Mary’s question establishes that at the time of the annunciation, she had no sexual relations with any male human being; therefore, the conception foretold could not proceed from human biological paternity.

---

### III. The Agency of Conception is the Holy Ghost and Divine Power

[L1] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] The Greek verb ἐπισκιάσει (*episkiasei*, future active indicative of ἐπισκιάζω, *episkiazō*, G1982) means "to overshadow, to cast a shade upon, to envelop in divine presence."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek phrase translated "is conceived" is τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν (*to gar en autē gennēthen*, aorist passive participle of γεννάω, *gennaō*, G1080, "to beget, to bear, to bring forth"), modified by the prepositional phrase ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*, "is of the Holy Ghost").
[L4] The origin and conception of the holy child was wrought by the divine overshadowing of the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos hagiou*), operating upon the womb of Mary, entirely replacing and excluding the biological seed or agency of a human male.

---

### IV. The Fulfillment of the Prophecy of the Virgin Birth

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] The Hebrew noun translated "virgin" is עַלְמָה (*‘almāh*, H5959, "a virgin, a young maiden of marriageable age who is unmarried and sexually untouched").
[L3] Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." In Matthew 1:23, the text employs the Greek noun ἡ παρθένος (*hē parthenos*, G3933, "the virgin"), an explicit technical designation for an unmarried woman who has preserved her chastity.
[L4] Prophecy required that the mother conceive while retaining the status of a virgin (*parthenos*); a conception occurring through the natural biological agency of a human male would extinguish that status and falsify the divine sign.

---

### V. Legal Paternity Versus Biological Origin in the Genealogies

[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli."
[L2] The Greek parenthetical participle phrase ὢν ὡς ἐνομίζετο (*ōn hōs enomizeto*) employs ἐνομίζετο (imperfect passive of νομίζω, *nomizō*, G3543, "to hold by custom, to deem, to reckon, to suppose according to custom or law").
[L3] Matthew 1:16 departs from the generational formula "A begat B" used in the preceding fifteen verses: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." In Matthew 1:16, the relative pronoun "of whom" is feminine singular in the Greek: ἐξ ἧς (*ex hēs*), referring exclusively to Mary, whereas every prior generation in the genealogy from verses 2 to 16 uses the active verb ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, "begat") applied to the male ancestor.
[L4] While Joseph was the customary and legal father according to the civic registers (*hōs enomizeto*), the scripture deliberately breaks the male begetting formula (*egennēsen*) at Joseph, attributing the birth exclusively to Mary (*ex hēs*), confirming that Joseph was not Christ's biological progenitor.

---

### DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew 1:18 exhibits that Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together (G4905, *synelthein*) with Joseph, and Matthew 1:25 exhibits that Joseph knew her not (G1097, *ginōskō*) till she brought forth her firstborn son.
2. Luke 1:34 exhibits that Mary had no carnal knowledge of a man (G1097, *ginōskō*), supported by Genesis 19:8 establishing that knowing a man signifies sexual relations.
3. Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:20 exhibit that the conception was directly effected by the overshadowing (G1982, *episkiazō*) of the Holy Ghost, and generated of the Holy Ghost (G1080, *gennaō*).
4. Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23 exhibit that Christ was conceived by an untouched virgin (H5959, *‘almāh*; G3933, *parthenos*) without the natural biological seed of a man.
5. Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16 exhibit that Joseph was the father only by custom and legal reckoning (G3543, *nomizō*), with the genealogy attributing physical birth solely to the mother (feminine relative pronoun *ex hēs*).
6. Christ did not have a biological father.

### CONCLUSION

The KJV text demonstrates with absolute precision that Jesus Christ did not have a biological father:
1. Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost prior to any physical union with Joseph (Matthew 1:18).

6. Joseph's relation to Jesus was strictly legal and social ("as was supposed", Luke 3:23), while physical begetting is attributed exclusively to Mary ("of whom was born Jesus", Matthew 1:16).

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures affirms that Christ was conceived in the womb of the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost without the agency of a human father, and therefore did not have a biological father.

### I. The Conception Occurred Before Joseph and Mary Came Together

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek temporal prepositional phrase translated "before they came together" contains πρίν (*prin*, G4250, "before, formerly") and συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, aorist active infinitive of συνέρχομαι, *synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together, to come together in cohabitation or conjugal union").
[L3] Matthew 1:25 confirms the absence of sexual intercourse until after the delivery: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Here "knew" renders ἔγινωσκεν (*eginōsken*, imperfect active of γινώσκω, *ginōskō*, G1097, used of carnal knowledge, as in Genesis 4:1).
[L4] Because Mary was already found with child prior to any conjugal union (*synelthein*) with Joseph, and Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth, Joseph was not the physical or biological generator of the child.

---

### II. Mary's Explicit Testimony of Carnal Inexperience

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] The Greek present active indicative verb γινώσκω (*ginōskō*, G1097, "to know, understand, perceive, have carnal relations with") is paired with the negative particle οὐ (*ou*, G3756, absolute negation) and ἄνδρα (*andra*, accusative singular of ἀνήρ, *anēr*, G435, "a male person, a husband, a man").
[L3] Genesis 19:8 exhibits the exact semantic force of knowing a man as sexual relations: "Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man."
[L4] Mary’s question establishes that at the time of the annunciation, she had no sexual relations with any male human being; therefore, the conception foretold could not proceed from human biological paternity.

---

### III. The Agency of Conception is the Holy Ghost and Divine Power

[L1] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] The Greek verb ἐπισκιάσει (*episkiasei*, future active indicative of ἐπισκιάζω, *episkiazō*, G1982) means "to overshadow, to cast a shade upon, to envelop in divine presence."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek phrase translated "is conceived" is τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν (*to gar en autē gennēthen*, aorist passive participle of γεννάω, *gennaō*, G1080, "to beget, to bear, to bring forth"), modified by the prepositional phrase ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*, "is of the Holy Ghost").
[L4] The origin and conception of the holy child was wrought by the divine overshadowing of the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos hagiou*), operating upon the womb of Mary, entirely replacing and excluding the biological seed or agency of a human male.

---

### IV. The Fulfillment of the Prophecy of the Virgin Birth

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] The Hebrew noun translated "virgin" is עַלְמָה (*‘almāh*, H5959, "a virgin, a young maiden of marriageable age who is unmarried and sexually untouched").
[L3] Matthew 1:22-23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." In Matthew 1:23, the text employs the Greek noun ἡ παρθένος (*hē parthenos*, G3933, "the virgin"), an explicit technical designation for an unmarried woman who has preserved her chastity.
[L4] Prophecy required that the mother conceive while retaining the status of a virgin (*parthenos*); a conception occurring through the natural biological agency of a human male would extinguish that status and falsify the divine sign.

---

### V. Legal Paternity Versus Biological Origin in the Genealogies

[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli."
[L2] The Greek parenthetical participle phrase ὢν ὡς ἐνομίζετο (*ōn hōs enomizeto*) employs ἐνομίζετο (imperfect passive of νομίζω, *nomizō*, G3543, "to hold by custom, to deem, to reckon, to suppose according to custom or law").
[L3] Matthew 1:16 departs from the generational formula "A begat B" used in the preceding fifteen verses: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." In Matthew 1:16, the relative pronoun "of whom" is feminine singular in the Greek: ἐξ ἧς (*ex hēs*), referring exclusively to Mary, whereas every prior generation in the genealogy from verses 2 to 16 uses the active verb ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, "begat") applied to the male ancestor.
[L4] While Joseph was the customary and legal father according to the civic registers (*hōs enomizeto*), the scripture deliberately breaks the male begetting formula (*egennēsen*) at Joseph, attributing the birth exclusively to Mary (*ex hēs*), confirming that Joseph was not Christ's biological progenitor.

---

### DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew 1:18 exhibits that Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together (G4905, *synelthein*) with Joseph, and Matthew 1:25 exhibits that Joseph knew her not (G1097, *ginōskō*) till she brought forth her firstborn son.
2. Luke 1:34 exhibits that Mary had no carnal knowledge of a man (G1097, *ginōskō*), supported by Genesis 19:8 establishing that knowing a man signifies sexual relations.
3. Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:20 exhibit that the conception was directly effected by the overshadowing (G1982, *episkiazō*) of the Holy Ghost, and generated of the Holy Ghost (G1080, *gennaō*).
4. Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23 exhibit that Christ was conceived by an untouched virgin (H5959, *‘almāh*; G3933, *parthenos*) without the natural biological seed of a man.
5. Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16 exhibit that Joseph was the father only by custom and legal reckoning (G3543, *nomizō*), with the genealogy attributing physical birth solely to the mother (feminine relative pronoun *ex hēs*).
6. Christ did not have a biological father.

"And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L1]
The challenger asserts under C4 that Luke 2:49 does not overturn Joseph's paternity because it refers to mission rather than physical loins. Yet Jesus uses the term "my Father" (*tou patros mou*) in immediate contrast to Mary's reference to Joseph in Luke 2:48 ("thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" [L3]). By subordinating the earthly parental claim to His divine origin and work, Christ Himself affirms that His true Father is God, consistent with Luke 1:35 where the child born of Mary is called "the Son of God" because He was conceived of the Holy Ghost [L3].

---

### CONCLUSION

The KJV text demonstrates with absolute precision that Jesus Christ did not have a biological father:
1. Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost prior to any physical union with Joseph (Matthew 1:18).
2. Mary herself attested that she knew not a man (Luke 1:34).
3. The conception was directly effected by the Holy Ghost overshadowing her (Luke 1:35, Matthew 1:20).
4. Isaiah's prophecy of the virginal conception was strictly fulfilled in this miraculous birth (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:22-23).
5. Joseph maintained complete sexual abstinence toward Mary until after the birth took place (Matthew 1:25).
6. Joseph's relation to Jesus was strictly legal and social ("as was supposed", Luke 3:23), while physical begetting is attributed exclusively to Mary ("of whom was born Jesus", Matthew 1:16).

Therefore, the standard reading is fully sustained: Christ did not have a biological father.

json.cr1:
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The standard reading of the Holy Scriptures affirms that Christ was conceived in the womb of the virgin Mary by the Holy Ghost without the agency of a human father, and therefore did not have a biological father.

### I. The Conception Occurred Before Joseph and Mary Came Together

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek temporal prepositional phrase translated "before they came together" contains πρίν (*prin*, G4250, "before, formerly") and συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, aorist active infinitive of συνέρχομαι, *synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together, to come together in cohabitation or conjugal union").
[L3] Matthew 1:25 confirms the absence of sexual intercourse until after the delivery: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Here "knew" renders ἔγινωσκεν (*eginōsken*, imperfect active of γινώσκω, *ginōskō*, G1097, used of carnal knowledge, as in Genesis 4:1).
[L4] Because Mary was already found with child prior to any conjugal union (*synelthein*) with Joseph, and Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth, Joseph was not the physical or biological generator of the child.

---

### II. Mary's Explicit Testimony of Carnal Inexperience

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] The Greek present active indicative verb γινώσκω (*ginōskō*, G1097, "to know, understand, perceive, have carnal relations with") is paired with the negative particle οὐ (*ou*, G3756, absolute negation) and ἄνδρα (*andra*, accusative singular of ἀνήρ, *anēr*, G435, "a male person, a husband, a man").
[L3] Genesis 19:8 exhibits the exact semantic force of knowing a man as sexual relations: "Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man."
[L4] Mary’s question establishes that at the time of the annunciation, she had no sexual relations with any male human being; therefore, the conception foretold could not proceed from human biological paternity.

---

### III. The Agency of Conception is the Holy Ghost and Divine Power

[L1] Luke 1:35: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] The Greek verb ἐπισκιάσει (*episkiasei*, future active indicative of ἐπισκιάζω, *episkiazō*, G1982) means "to overshadow, to cast a shade upon, to envelop in divine presence."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek phrase translated "is conceived" is τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν (*to gar en autē gennēthen*, aorist passive participle of γεννάω, *gennaō*, G1080, "to beget, to bear, to bring forth"), modified by the prepositional phrase ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos estin hagiou*, "is of the Holy Ghost").
[L4] The origin and conception of the holy child was wrought by the divine overshadowing of the Holy Ghost (*ek pneumatos hagiou*), operating upon the womb of Mary, entirely replacing and excluding the biological seed or agency of a human male.

---

### IV. The Fulfillment of the Prophecy of the Virgin Birth

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] The Hebrew noun translated "virgin" is עַלְמָה (*‘almāh*, H5959, "a virgin, a young maiden of marriageable age who is unmarried and sexually untouched").

"And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted [thither]." [L1]
The challenger argues under C4 that *nomizō* in Acts 16:13 ("prayer was wont to be made") indicates customary practice, so Luke 3:23 ("as was supposed") merely reflects ordinary custom rather than an erroneous or non-biological assumption. But *nomizō* G3543 means "to reckon by custom, suppose". In Luke 3:23, Luke uses "(as was supposed)" (*hōs enomizeto*) precisely because Luke has already revealed the secret, divine reality in Luke 1:34-35 that Mary knew no man and conceived by the Holy Ghost [L3]. The public, customary supposition that Jesus was the biological son of Joseph was an external assumption contrary to the factual supernatural conception Luke narrated.

ANSWER: John 6:42 -- D4 / D5 --
"And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" [L1]
The challenger argues under C4 that the Jews' words "whose father and mother we know" confirm Joseph's paternity. But this statement reflects the unbelieving perception of the Jews of Capernaum who murmured at His divine origin ("how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" [L1]). Their ignorance of His supernatural conception does not establish biological paternity; rather, their earthly assumption confirms what Luke 3:23 states: it was only "as was supposed" by the general public [L3].

ANSWER: Matthew 1:19 -- D1 / D5 --
"Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." [L1]
The challenger argues under C5 that Joseph being Mary's "husband" suggests natural marital relations. But Matthew 1:19 explicitly shows that when Mary was found with child, Joseph was minded to put her away privily precisely because he knew he was not the father of the unborn child. Had Joseph been the biological father through marital intercourse, he would have had no cause to seek a divorce or fear a public scandal. His intention to put her away confirms that Mary's pregnancy was conceived without him.

ANSWER: Matthew 1:24 -- D1 / D5 --
"Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" [L1]
The challenger argues under C5 that taking Mary unto him as wife at Matthew 1:24 means they came together in normal procreative relations. But Matthew 1:25 immediately qualifies this taking: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" [L3]. Joseph took Mary into his home as his wife to protect her reputation and obey the angel, but strictly abstained from carnal knowledge of her until after the child was born. Therefore, taking her as wife involved no sexual intercourse prior to the birth.

ANSWER: Genesis 4:1 -- D1 / D5 / D6 --
"And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." [L1]
The challenger argues under C5 that because natural conception in Genesis 4:1 occurs when a husband "knew" his wife, Joseph's marriage to Mary implies the same natural order. On the contrary, Genesis 4:1 confirms that biblical "knowing" signifies sexual relations that produce conception. Matthew 1:25 states that Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" [L3]. The explicit negation ("knew her not") during the entire period of gestation conclusively excludes Joseph from having the carnal knowledge that begets a child.

ANSWER: Galatians 4:4 -- D3 / D6 --
"But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," [L1]
The challenger argues under C3 that "made under the law" demands a biological father to establish legal pedigree. However, Galatians 4:4 pointedly says God sent forth His Son "made of a woman" (*genomenon ek gynaikos*), conspicuously omitting any human father in the physical origin of the Son. The Son is sent forth from God, takes human flesh entirely from the woman, and is placed under the law through His birth into the covenant people and legal adoption into Joseph's Davidic house, fully fulfilling the law without a biological earthly father.

ANSWER: Luke 2:49 -- D4 / D5 --
"And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L1]
The challenger asserts under C4 that Luke 2:49 does not overturn Joseph's paternity because it refers to mission rather than physical loins. Yet Jesus uses the term "my Father" (*tou patros mou*) in immediate contrast to Mary's reference to Joseph in Luke 2:48 ("thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" [L3]). By subordinating the earthly parental claim to His divine origin and work, Christ Himself affirms that His true Father is God, consistent with Luke 1:35 where the child born of Mary is called "the Son of God" because He was conceived of the Holy Ghost [L3].

---

### CONCLUSION

The KJV text demonstrates with absolute precision that Jesus Christ did not have a biological father:
1. Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost prior to any physical union with Joseph (Matthew 1:18).
2. Mary herself attested that she knew not a man (Luke 1:34).
3. The conception was directly effected by the Holy Ghost overshadowing her (Luke 1:35, Matthew 1:20).
4. Isaiah's prophecy of the virginal conception was strictly fulfilled in this miraculous birth (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:22-23).
5. Joseph maintained complete sexual abstinence toward Mary until after the birth took place (Matthew 1:25).
6. Joseph's relation to Jesus was strictly legal and social ("as was supposed", Luke 3:23), while physical begetting is attributed exclusively to Mary ("of whom was born Jesus", Matthew 1:16).

Therefore, the standard reading is fully sustained: Christ did not have a biological father.

You are ONE of three INDEPENDENT judges of a completed debate. You have not seen the other judges and you will not. Judge only what is in the transcript below. You are bound by the same layer rules as all debate participants, and by the same rulebook as every other judge of this debate.

Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none
  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none
  "reasoning": string -- the worked grading: the RESULT line, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE, both standings with their justification, both conceded-link itemizations, COLLISION POINTS, the citation check, OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, DEFENDER CHAIN MARK and CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK, in the forms the rulebook below gives, one per line (newlines escaped as \n inside the JSON string)
}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. The SEPTUAGINT SCAN line lists any round that rests a reading on the Greek Old Testament: name it at the citation check.
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 1: no verbatim quote found
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 2: no verbatim quote found
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 3: absent from its quote: christ, romans, through, mother, bodily, substance, while, joseph, davidic, house, luke, provides, legal, pedigree, fathers, numbers, step, link || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 4: no verbatim quote found
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 5: absent from its quote: because, mary, already, found, child, prior, conjugal, union, synelthein, joseph, until, after, birth, physical, biological, generator || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ANY, which its quote lacks
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 6: no verbatim quote found
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 1: absent from its quote: challenger, infers, action, luke, matthew, merely, empowering, presence, covenantal, mark, exclude, male, biological, procreation || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 2: absent from its quote: challenger, infers, isaiah, ONLY, denotes, natural, days, king, ahaz, signify, miraculous, apart, human, male || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ONLY, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 3: absent from its quote: challenger, infers, descent, david, requires, physical, male, progenitor, excludes, maternal, bodily || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 4: absent from its quote: challenger, infers, luke, refers, ONLY, public, WITHOUT, denying, joseph, true, biological || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ONLY, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 5: absent from its quote: challenger, infers, allow, joseph, biologically, begotten, jesus, during, betrothal || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
SEPTUAGINT SCAN (computed by the system, not by a model): no round rests a reading on the Septuagint.

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<the round that holds the quoted ANSWER; with ANSWER: NONE, the answering side's round for that press>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose fit rests on a fact that the quoted 1611 rows, read together line upon line (Isaiah 28:10), do not give does not meet the press. One verse read alone does not give a contested fact. Grade it MISSES and name the fact. Quoting the rows that together give the fact, each step in a row's own words, meets it. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. Pressure from the challenger's texts alone is not a withdrawal (w); a witness the side's later rounds leave unanswered is graded under UNANSWERED WITNESS and at the COLLISION POINTS. An UNEXHIBITED link counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings, never toward w. BROKEN AT COLLISION: a defender link graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN on the COLLISION POINTS lines; k = their number. A grade that rests on a witness left unanswered counts only when that witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (md_notes_rulings 392).
BROKEN-1: k >= 1 -- a listed defender link refuted from the text.
BROKEN-2: 2w > n, OR the keystone link is WITHDRAWN.
PARTIAL-1: w >= 1.
PARTIAL-2: DEFENSE STANDING is COLLAPSED.
HELD-1: none of the above.
STANDINGS ARE GRADED BY THEIR OWN RULES ONLY. DEFENSE STANDING and CHALLENGE STANDING are each decided by their own definitions below and by nothing else. Any standing is legal with any CLAUSE: the clauses are tried in order and the first match wins, so a COLLAPSED standing under BROKEN-1, BROKEN-2 or PARTIAL-1 is correct and changes no clause. Never choose a standing, a count or a clause to agree with another line, a check or an expected result.
A SIDE WITH A COUNTED LINK IS NOT SELF-SUPPORTED. If CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, DEFENSE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge; if CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, CHALLENGE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge. SELF-SUPPORTED requires a count of 0 for that side: every premise listed against it exhibited its footing or was VOID.
Line 1: the verdict word first (HELD, PARTIAL or BROKEN), then 2-4 sentences with [L1][L2][L3][L4] tags.
Line 2, exactly: RESULT: DEFENDER WINS | CHALLENGER WINS | UNDERDETERMINED -- one sentence a reader with no background understands. BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS. Otherwise the RESULT is your judgment (Commitments 7 and 8): DEFENDER WINS when the verses of the record, read together line upon line, support the chain of the defender against the chain of the challenger; UNDERDETERMINED when, read together, they leave the topic open. The sentence gives the reason.
Line 3, exactly: CLAUSE: <BROKEN-1 | BROKEN-2 | PARTIAL-1 | PARTIAL-2 | HELD-1> -- n=<n> w=<w> k=<k>

Then SIX MORE mandatory lines, exactly in these forms:
KEYSTONE: D<n> -- WITHDRAWN | BROKEN | STANDS -- name the LAST declared link, Dn, which is the conclusion link, and give its state. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. A defender link that a premise of the list closing [DR2] presses is not any other link: it takes a graded D<i> vs C<j> line for the challenger link it collides with, in whatever grade you judge; a D<i>: STANDS line alone does not grade it and is sent back (pkgUND). An UNDERDETERMINED grade gives, after GROUND:, [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words both readings rest on>" and what the record leaves open. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. CARRIED BY shows that the pressed verse itself carries the MEANS sentence; K-FC, a TRIAL check, finds its words in that verse as the KJV reads it. A MEANS its own verse does not carry is no ground for a forced link. FAILS names what in the answer fails, its own reading; a verse does not fail. K-FF, a TRIAL check, returns for cure a FAILS that is only the words of a verse the answer quotes. A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). STRAINED = the chain is built but one or more load-bearing links float: a link floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers; the mark names the layers exhibited and the layer lacking; it stands only under charity. SLACK = the side advanced no coherent chain of its own: objections without a constructed reading, or a construction that never cohered. Each mark describes ONLY how well that side built its own chain. It is descriptive, not a verdict. It MUST NOT change DEFENSE STANDING, CHALLENGE STANDING, CONCEDED LINKS, CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE or the top-line verdict. A FOOTED chain is fully compatible with its side losing the debate; a SLACK chain is fully compatible with its side winning it.

POSTURE FOR ACCEPTANCE You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given. ### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence. The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step. ### Commitment 2. I repair nothing. You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. Any inference of your own shows two lower layers, as a debater's must. ### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words. Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. ### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides. The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line. ### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral. A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. A verse pressed with no listed premise behind it is not a witness. A premise carries at most eight witnesses. ### Commitment 6. I void only by quoting. You rule a listed premise VOID only by quoting the words of its charge that go beyond its quote, and naming the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Paraphrase, reordering and dropped words are not stronger. [L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek temporal prepositional phrase translated "before they came together" contains πρίν (*prin*, G4250, "before, formerly") and συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, aorist active infinitive of συνέρχομαι, *synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together, to come together in cohabitation or conjugal union").

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

By subordinating the earthly parental claim to His divine origin and work, Christ Himself affirms that His true Father is God, consistent with Luke 1:35 where the child born of Mary is called "the Son of God" because He was conceived of the Holy Ghost [L3].

---

### CONCLUSION

The KJV text demonstrates with absolute precision that Jesus Christ did not have a biological father:
1. Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost prior to any physical union with Joseph (Matthew 1:18).
2. Mary herself attested that she knew not a man (Luke 1:34).
3. The conception was directly effected by the Holy Ghost overshadowing her (Luke 1:35, Matthew 1:20).
4. Isaiah's prophecy of the virginal conception was strictly fulfilled in this miraculous birth (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:22-23).
5. Joseph maintained complete sexual abstinence toward Mary until after the birth took place (Matthew 1:25).
6. Joseph's relation to Jesus was strictly legal and social ("as was supposed", Luke 3:23), while physical begetting is attributed exclusively to Mary ("of whom was born Jesus", Matthew 1:16).

Therefore, the standard reading is fully sustained: Christ did not have a biological father.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<the round that holds the quoted ANSWER; with ANSWER: NONE, the answering side's round for that press>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose fit rests on a fact that the quoted 1611 rows, read together line upon line (Isaiah 28:10), do not give does not meet the press. One verse read alone does not give a contested fact. Grade it MISSES and name the fact. Quoting the rows that together give the fact, each step in a row's own words, meets it. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. His intention to put her away confirms that Mary's pregnancy was conceived without him.

ANSWER: Matthew 1:24 -- D1 / D5 --
"Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" [L1]
The challenger argues under C5 that taking Mary unto him as wife at Matthew 1:24 means they came together in normal procreative relations. But Matthew 1:25 immediately qualifies this taking: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" [L3]. Joseph took Mary into his home as his wife to protect her reputation and obey the angel, but strictly abstained from carnal knowledge of her until after the child was born. Therefore, taking her as wife involved no sexual intercourse prior to the birth.

ANSWER: Genesis 4:1 -- D1 / D5 / D6 --
"And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." [L1]
The challenger argues under C5 that because natural conception in Genesis 4:1 occurs when a husband "knew" his wife, Joseph's marriage to Mary implies the same natural order. On the contrary, Genesis 4:1 confirms that biblical "knowing" signifies sexual relations that produce conception. Matthew 1:25 states that Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" [L3]. The explicit negation ("knew her not") during the entire period of gestation conclusively excludes Joseph from having the carnal knowledge that begets a child.

ANSWER: Galatians 4:4 -- D3 / D6 --
"But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," [L1]
The challenger argues under C3 that "made under the law" demands a biological father to establish legal pedigree. However, Galatians 4:4 pointedly says God sent forth His Son "made of a woman" (*genomenon ek gynaikos*), conspicuously omitting any human father in the physical origin of the Son. The Son is sent forth from God, takes human flesh entirely from the woman, and is placed under the law through His birth into the covenant people and legal adoption into Joseph's Davidic house, fully fulfilling the law without a biological earthly father.

ANSWER: Luke 2:49 -- D4 / D5 --
"And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L1]
The challenger asserts under C4 that Luke 2:49 does not overturn Joseph's paternity because it refers to mission rather than physical loins. Yet Jesus uses the term "my Father" (*tou patros mou*) in immediate contrast to Mary's reference to Joseph in Luke 2:48 ("thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" [L3]). By subordinating the earthly parental claim to His divine origin and work, Christ Himself affirms that His true Father is God, consistent with Luke 1:35 where the child born of Mary is called "the Son of God" because He was conceived of the Holy Ghost [L3].

---

### CONCLUSION

The KJV text demonstrates with absolute precision that Jesus Christ did not have a biological father:
1. Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost prior to any physical union with Joseph (Matthew 1:18).
2. Mary herself attested that she knew not a man (Luke 1:34).
3. The conception was directly effected by the Holy Ghost overshadowing her (Luke 1:35, Matthew 1:20).
4. Isaiah's prophecy of the virginal conception was strictly fulfilled in this miraculous birth (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:22-23).
5. Joseph maintained complete sexual abstinence toward Mary until after the birth took place (Matthew 1:25).
6. Joseph's relation to Jesus was strictly legal and social ("as was supposed", Luke 3:23), while physical begetting is attributed exclusively to Mary ("of whom was born Jesus", Matthew 1:16).

Therefore, the standard reading is fully sustained: Christ did not have a biological father.

THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<the round that holds the quoted ANSWER; with ANSWER: NONE, the answering side's round for that press>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". An answer whose fit rests on a fact that the quoted 1611 rows, read together line upon line (Isaiah 28:10), do not give does not meet the press. One verse read alone does not give a contested fact. Grade it MISSES and name the fact. Quoting the rows that together give the fact, each step in a row's own words, meets it. MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. Pressure from the challenger's texts alone is not a withdrawal (w); a witness the side's later rounds leave unanswered is graded under UNANSWERED WITNESS and at the COLLISION POINTS. An UNEXHIBITED link counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings, never toward w. BROKEN AT COLLISION: a defender link graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN on the COLLISION POINTS lines; k = their number. BROKEN-1: k >= 1 -- a listed defender link refuted from the text.
BROKEN-2: 2w > n, OR the keystone link is WITHDRAWN.
PARTIAL-1: w >= 1.
PARTIAL-2: DEFENSE STANDING is COLLAPSED.
HELD-1: none of the above.
STANDINGS ARE GRADED BY THEIR OWN RULES ONLY. DEFENSE STANDING and CHALLENGE STANDING are each decided by their own definitions below and by nothing else. Any standing is legal with any CLAUSE: the clauses are tried in order and the first match wins, so a COLLAPSED standing under BROKEN-1, BROKEN-2 or PARTIAL-1 is correct and changes no clause. COLLISION POINTS: the label on its own line, then one entry per line covering every defender link D1..Dn, none omitted.
