A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason; a BROKEN grade gives it in layers: [L1] <reference> "<KJV words>" | [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>, <gloss>) when it turns on a word's meaning | [L3] <reference> "<KJV words>" (Commitment 13)>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. A defender link that a premise of the list closing [DR2] presses is not any other link: it takes a graded D<i> vs C<j> line for the challenger link it collides with, in whatever grade you judge; a D<i>: STANDS line alone does not grade it and is sent back (pkgUND). An UNDERDETERMINED grade gives, after GROUND:, [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words both readings rest on>" and what the record leaves open. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the answer's own words that fail to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round: its reading, not only the words of a verse it quotes>" -- CARRIED BY: "<the words of the pressed witness's own verse that state its MEANS sentence, quoted from the KJV>" -- GROUND: [L1] <reference> "<the KJV words the answer cannot agree with>" | [L2] <word> (<Strong's number>, <gloss>), when the break turns on a word's meaning | [L3] <reference> "<KJV words>", for any cross-reference relied on (Commitment 13). Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. CARRIED BY shows that the pressed verse itself carries the MEANS sentence; K-FC, a TRIAL check, finds its words in that verse as the KJV reads it. A MEANS its own verse does not carry is no ground for a forced link. FAILS names what in the answer fails, its own reading; a verse does not fail. K-FF, a TRIAL check, returns for cure a FAILS that is only the words of a verse the answer quotes. A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. The KJV text demonstrates with absolute precision that Jesus Christ did not have a biological father:
1. Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost prior to any physical union with Joseph (Matthew 1:18).
2. Mary herself attested that she knew not a man (Luke 1:34).
3. The conception was directly effected by the Holy Ghost overshadowing her (Luke 1:35, Matthew 1:20).
4. Isaiah's prophecy of the virginal conception was strictly fulfilled in this miraculous birth (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:22-23).
5. Joseph maintained complete sexual abstinence toward Mary until after the birth took place (Matthew 1:25).
6. Joseph's relation to Jesus was strictly legal and social ("as was supposed", Luke 3:23), while physical begetting is attributed exclusively to Mary ("of whom was born Jesus", Matthew 1:16).

Therefore, the standard reading is fully sustained: Christ did not have a biological father.
